full_judgment:
AmiruI Kabir Chowdhury J: This appeal has been preferred by the defendants-the Secretary, Ministry of Food and others against the judgment and decree passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in civil Revision No. 2170 of 1998 on 7-12-1998 discharging the Rule thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 16-11-1997 in Title Appeal No. 25 of 1997 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayanganj who allowed the appeal in part reversing those passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Bandar, Narayanganj dated 20-2-1997 in Title Suit No. 4 of 1996 deereeing the suit. 

 5. Upon hearing the parties, the trial Court decreed the suit on 20-2-1997 in favour of the plaintiff-respondents to the extent of 3.79 acres of land. The Government being aggrieved preferred an appeal and the plaintiff-respondent also filed cross objection. The Appellate Court dismissed the appeal by decreeing the suit for more area of land being 4.17 acres of land. Against the aforesaid judgment of the lower Appellate Court the leave petitioners moved the High Court Division and the Rule obtained in the Revision was discharged. Hence is this appeal. 

 6. Leave was granted to consider the submissions of the appellant that the High Court Division committed error of law in not considering that upon the averments as made in the plaint the very auction sale was void but the learned Judge of the High Court Division without considering the said aspect of the case committed error of law in affirming the findings and decisions as arrived at by the Courts below and that the High Court Division did not take into consideration that the plaintiff-respondent failed to discharge its initial onus as regards his alleged enjoyment and possession in the suit property inasmuch as the suit property is part of the godown, the jetty, yard and the office building of the appellant No. 1 and that the appellant being added as defendant No.4 on 24-11-1996 the suit itself was decreed on 22-1-1997 without allowing the added defendant, that is the appellant, two month's time in view of non-issuance of any notice under section 80(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure by the plaintiff-respondent and, as such, there being gross violation of mandatory provision of section 80 of the Code, the trial Court as well as the Court of appeal below committed illegality in not dismissing the suit. 

 7. In support of the appeal Mr Abdur Razaque Khan, learned Additional Attorney-General, reiterated the submissions made by him at the time of hearing the leave petition. He further submits that there being violation of the provision of section 80(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure the defendant-appellant has been seriously prejudiced being deprived of the chance of contesting the suit, legitimate period allowed under the law being not given to the defendant and as a result of which the defendant could not file written statement and, therefore, ex parte decree had been passed against the defendant to the serious peril of the interests of the appellant. 

 8. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Senior Advocate opposed the appeal, contending, inter alia, that the trial Court considered the facts and circumstances and evidence on record including written statement of the contesting defendant who contested the suit. He further submits that the lower appellate Court considered the quantum of land purchased by the plaintiff from individual plots and also the quantum of land acquired from the individual plots and found that the plaintiffs succeeded to prove his claim of 4.17 acres of land and, therefore, decreed the same accordingly, in his favour. 

 10. Since we have decided to send the suit on remand, we do not like to embark upon the merits and demerits of the submissions of the parties advanced before us. It appears that on 24-11-1996 plaintiff-respondents filed an application under Order 1, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying to implead the appellant as defendant No.4 and the prayer was allowed accordingly, impleading the appellant as defendant No. 4 amending the plaint. On 22-1-1997 the trial Court issued summons upon the added defendant No.4 that is, the appellant, fixing 28-1-1997 for service return and by order dated 28-1-1997 on perusal of the service return of summons, fixed 3-2-1997 for  peremptory hearing and ultimately by Order No. XXIV dated 20-2-1997 pronounced the judgment allowing ex parte decree against the appellant. 

 13. We have already noticed that the appellant 1 was impleaded as defendant on 24-11-1996 and the suit itself has been decreed ex parte against the appellant 1 on 20-2-1997. There is nothing in the plaint to indicate that any notice as required under section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure were issued/served. It thus appears that mandatory period of three months has not been allowed to the appellant to enable it to submit its written statement. In this view of the matter, we find substance in the submissions made by the learned Additional Attorney-General and on this score alone the suit, according to us, is required to be sent back to the trial Court on remand directing the trial Court to give reasonable time to defendant No.4 to submit written statement and the trial Court shall proceed in accordance with law. 

 In the result, the appeal is allowed. The judgment and order of the High Court Division, and the judgment and decree passed by the Additional District Judge and the Assistant Judge are hereby set aside. Title Suit No. 4 of 1996 is sent back on remand to the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Bandar, Narayanganj for disposal as directed above. The appellant No.1, Secretary, Ministry of Food, Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh do pay cost of Taka 3,000 in favour of the plaintiff- respondent No. 1 within two months from the date of receipt of this order by the trial Court, in default, this appeal shall stand dismissed.
